title: Season removal changes the selected GJ 433 residual period in some HARPS fits
abstract: We audit a previously selected 35.23-day GJ 433 residual in 86 HARPS RVBank version 02 exposures. Eight season removals leave main SERVAL scan peaks between 35.21 and 35.33 days, with fixed-wave amplitudes of 1.77 to 2.52 m/s. Some DRS and trend controls select other periods. Removal of the final season leaves 36.2 percent of the full fixed-wave squared-error decrease. Conditional coherent-wave sign tests give lower-tail fractions of 0.064, 0.031 and 0.021 with 1-, 30- and 90-day groups. These model-dependent fractions do not establish time variation. The audit shows uneven support and period sensitivity. It does not find a new planet or resolve stellar activity, trend error or shared artifacts. Both reductions use the same spectra. No independent instrument confirmation is obtained. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Fixed-wave fit improvement and selected scan period after each season is removed. The baseline includes a quadratic trend and fixed 7.3705- and 36.059-day waves. SERVAL and DRS share the same spectra.

citations.reason: Supplies the prior residual period and data source. This audit adds season removal; no code is reused.
